solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Writer's block coming on? Apply liquid!

indicators.note: the writer's word comes on after the block, joining it at the end

parts.note: a dam blocks a river
a pen is the writer's tool, standing for the writer

explanation.surface: A frustrated author with writer's block is told to splash some water about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' reads as the familiar creative slump, but the two words split apart, and 'coming on' puts the writer after the block.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something is to apply liquid to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: River's current flowing round Middle-earth

indicators.note: the current word flows round the river's letter, enclosing it

parts.note: topical means current, of present interest
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A Tolkien-style picture of a river's current winding round Middle-earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-earth' suggests Tolkien, but here it is the region round the Equator: the middle of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics form the belt round the middle of the globe, so this adjective describes that equatorial zone, cryptically.

clue.text: Policeman reported as being wasted on drink

indicators.note: reported means heard rather than read, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: blew means squandered (wasted) and bottle stands for drink, giving blew bottle

explanation.surface: A policeman is said to have been squandering money on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUEBOTTLE is old British slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British slang term for a uniformed police constable, from the blue uniform.

clue.text: Legal officer with cops cut off at both ends amid angry riots

indicators.note: amid means the trimmed police word sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
angry riots are wild and disordered, so the letters of riots are rearranged
the word for cops loses its first and last letters

parts.note: cops are the police

explanation.surface: A lawyer turns up alongside the police in the middle of furious rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry' signals the anagram of the riots letters, and 'amid' sets the trimmed cops word in their middle, so the anagram is split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a solicitor is a lawyer who advises clients and prepares legal documents.

clue.text: He's not out to get bank transfer system overhauled

indicators.note: overhauled is taken as turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: BACS is the UK's automated bank payment clearing system

explanation.surface: A batsman who isn't out gets the bank's payment system revamped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhauled' reverses BACS, the British bank transfer system. 'He's not out' sounds like cricket, but it means a worker who isn't out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker keeps working when colleagues walk out, so he is not out on strike.

clue.text: Joke to needle Asian region

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
to needle or jab is to poke at someone

explanation.surface: Telling a joke to needle someone from part of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjab is a region split between India and Pakistan in South Asia.

clue.text: Rejection of bottom-pinching old royal

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the royal word grips the bottom word inside it

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish coin, whose name means royal
butt is slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: A cheeky old royal pinches someone's bottom and is rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: The real was an old Spanish coin; its name is Spanish for 'royal', which is how 'old royal' gets there.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a refutation or rejection of an argument or claim.

clue.text: Edge of asphalt on shed tears — finish off cursory coat of paint

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to cry is to shed tears

indicators.note: finish off means the end of the word is taken off

parts.note: a lick of paint is a quick cursory coat

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over a hastily painted patch of tarmac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat of paint' looks like the definition, but 'cursory coat' gives LICK, which 'finish off' cuts to LIC; only 'paint' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a common type of synthetic paint, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: He's not in gear, the fool

indicators.note: the letters of he's are not in the clothes word, so they are removed

parts.note: gear is clothes, what one wears
the letters of he's, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in neutral is dismissed as an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in gear' sounds like a car, but 'gear' is CLOTHES and HES is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: One of these had homophone cut off

indicators.note: the word homophone says that these words are said aloud

parts.note: one of these is a clue, and had is shortened to 'd, giving a clue'd

explanation.surface: A puzzle remark that one clue once had a homophone removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These' are the clues themselves: 'a clue'd' (a clue had) said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or shut off, as an artery or a view is cut off.

clue.text: Does this sausage go with Italian beer?

indicators.note: with joins the energy word to the beer, one beside the other

parts.note: go, as in energy, is pep
Peroni is a well-known Italian lager brand

explanation.surface: A question of whether a spicy sausage pairs well with Italian lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American cured sausage, common on pizza.

clue.text: Boom's gone into reverse — you must offload prime item of jewellery

indicators.note: the boom word goes into reverse, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a jib is the projecting arm or boom of a crane

indicators.note: offload prime means the first letter of you is dropped

explanation.surface: An economic boom reverses, so you must sell off your best jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom' looks economic but is JIB, which 'gone into reverse' turns to BIJ; 'offload prime' drops Y from YOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijou is French for a jewel or trinket, used in English for a small elegant thing.

clue.text: North American preference — not frozen kind of chip

indicators.note: not means the frozen word is left out of the preference

parts.note: a choice is a preference
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: North Americans prefer their chips fresh rather than frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not frozen' looks descriptive, but it takes ICE out of CHOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, typically served with melted cheese.

clue.text: Occupy hotel, coming in later

indicators.note: coming in means the hotel letter enters the phrase for later

parts.note: in a bit means later
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone will take a hotel room, checking in a little later.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in or occupy it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Prison head sent down with no means to get out of cell — that's what it's all about!

indicators.note: the first letter of the prison word is sent down to its bottom, as this is a down clue

parts.note: chokey is British slang for prison
O, a zero, stands for no or nothing

parts.words: means to get out of cell
parts.note: a key is the means of unlocking a cell

explanation.surface: A prison governor is jailed with no key to escape his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOKEY is British slang for prison. The HOKEY COKEY is a British party dance whose chorus ends 'that's what it's all about!'
explanation.definitionFit: The closing line of the chorus of this group dance song identifies it.

clue.text: An extra bed covering retains a bit of heat in heavy snowfall

indicators.note: retains means the bed drape holds the bit of heat inside it

parts.note: a valance is a short drape round the base of a bed

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its first letter

explanation.surface: An additional blanket keeps some warmth in during a blizzard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retains' puts H, from 'a bit of heat', inside VALANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow sliding down a mountain, a heavy fall of snow.

clue.text: Vital to mock 'cool' jerks — but it can be wounding if it hits home

definitions.text: it can be wounding if it hits home

indicators.note: jerks means sharp jolts, so the letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: Mocking 'cool' idiots feels essential, but such mockery can wound if it lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' looks like the idiots being mocked; it is the anagram signal for the fifteen letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrol bomb thrown at a house injures people when it strikes its target.

clue.text: Lifeless bank suppressing ridicule

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the bank word encloses the ridicule word

parts.note: a mound is a bank of earth
to rib is to tease or ridicule

explanation.surface: A dead-looking bank keeps a lid on public mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means near death, and so figuratively lacking vitality or energy.

clue.text: Circus folk wound cetacean surfacing

indicators.note: in a down clue surfacing means rising up, so the letters are read upwards

parts.note: to stab is to wound
an orca is a killer whale, a cetacean

explanation.surface: Performers get hurt as a whale breaks the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfacing' reverses STAB plus ORCA, reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats perform tumbling and balancing acts, classic circus performers.

clue.text: Rough end of untreated wood

parts.note: raw means unprocessed, untreated
deal is sawn fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: The rough end of a plank of unfinished timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough end' is from the idiom 'the rough end of the stick', unfair treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment is the rough end of the stick in idiom, a synonymous phrase.

clue.text: Succeed with effort in cold

indicators.note: with joins the success word to the effort word, side by side

parts.note: to win is to succeed
a try is an effort or attempt

explanation.surface: Achieving victory through hard work in the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather is cold, frosty, like winter.

clue.text: Stories to tell in turn, entertaining sailors

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the reversed word holds the sailors inside
in turn means the telling word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to tell is to say
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Taking turns telling stories to amuse a group of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' looks like taking turns, but it means the telling word is read backwards, giving YAS to wrap round the sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarns are long tales, often embellished, especially sailors' tales.

clue.text: Head of state Queen Elizabeth going around gardens with barbecue implement?

indicators.note: going around means the outer letters surround the garden name
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: The Queen strolls round her gardens holding a barbecue tool.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the famous botanic gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer holds pieces of meat for grilling, used at a barbecue; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Mounting objections end

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing up, so the letters are read upwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Growing objections bring something to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is a short remaining end, as of a cigarette or pencil.

clue.text: Extra payout for principal of bank, having responsibility

indicators.note: the principal letter of a word is its first

parts.note: an onus is a responsibility or burden

explanation.surface: A bank chief gets an extra payout for carrying responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like a bank boss; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra payment on top of normal wages.

clue.text: Body part seen during washing

indicators.note: seen during means the letters show up inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A part of the body glimpsed while someone washes.
explanation.definitionFit: The front of the lower leg, below the knee, is a part of the body.

clue.text: Problem-free? That can't be said of falling currency!

definitions.meaning: something problem-free is easy, causes no bother

definitions.text: That can't be said of falling currency!
definitions.meaning: a falling currency, the Russian rouble then sliding, could not be called not the rouble

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ROUBLE, the phrase would say the currency is not the rouble, which could not be said of the falling Russian currency of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is easily done, causing no bother, matches being problem-free.

clue.text: Socially awkward to leave half of dinner on plate

indicators.note: on joins the remaining half to the plate word, placed beside it
half of dinner leaves, so its first half is dropped

parts.note: a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: A shy diner leaves half the meal untouched on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being geeky and lacking social skills is a stereotype of awkwardness.

clue.text: Prepare herb tea to get inspiration

indicators.note: to prepare is to make ready, so the letters of herb tea are made into a new order

explanation.surface: Brewing a herbal tea to find creative inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' looks creative, but here it means drawing in breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration literally means inhaling, so to get inspiration is to draw breath.
